questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place where I spoke the language and where they offered classes that I found interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there were informational meetings and online guides.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was greeted at the airport and had a meeting with an Erasmus adviser, as well as an academic adviser

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many options were available. Always with flat-mates and own bedroom, but typically shared kitchen and sometimes shared bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were kitchen in all apartments and cafeteria's on campus, as well as a little cafe/restaurant in the student village.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The apartments are not beautiful, but everything that you could ever need is there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had looked at the course catalogue before the exchange and then when I arrived at the destination, I had a meeting with my academic adviser and he booked me a spot on those classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could talk to both an academic adviser and an Erasmus adviser, if you needed to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a very straightforward process, so don't worry about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was studying my electives while on exchange, so I chose some entry-level courses in different schools than my typical one, so as to broaden my horizons.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EL2512 - The Tragedy of Knowledge, DR152C - Magic, Mystery, Spells and Potions in the Ancient World and AT1502 - Introduction to Anthropology 2: Questions of Diversity.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I particularly enjoyed my anthropology course, as it is something that I have always wanted to study and it was very nice to finally have that opportunity.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I encountered any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out for dinner or going to the movie theatre was less expensive than I had expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds. They have so many "societies" or clubs that it doesn't matter what you like, there is a club for you, as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Taking trips, whether overnight or day trips. It is a great way to learn more about the culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely the Loch Ness and Isle of Skye. But more locally the Bullards of Buchen was breathtaking, and Duffie Park in central Aberdeen is a lovely place to spend an afternoon.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, I didn't feel that big of a difference.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Scots are very friendly and always easy to talk to. However, they might feel as though they don't want to go exploring the country with you (same as you typically don't explore the country that you live in very much).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It took a while to get used to the fact that they drive on the other side of the road, so I missed some busses because I was standing on the wrong side of the road and was very scared of getting hit by cars at first.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness and how easy-going they are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try new things every chance you get, talk to as many people as you can and enjoy it. It will be over before you know it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Doric accent can be hard to understand, but they are very nice and will slow their speech for you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting and bonding with people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from all of my friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you have the change to go on exchange, take it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
